checklist.detail: Installed `claude --version` reported 2.1.280 before the real PTY run.
PtyConfig emitted --dangerously-skip-permissions and --permission-mode bypassPermissions; the TUI showed bypass permissions on.
PtyConfig emitted --model opus and --effort high; transcript assistant messages recorded claude-opus-5-5 and the TUI showed high effort.
Injected worker startup prompt named the Cassy worker role; the root turn called coordination whoami and task mine.
Root turn discovered mcp__cas tools through ToolSearch, then called coordination whoami and task mine.
Follow-up turn called coordination whoami and task mine a second time in the same session.

Disposable project hook canaries created session-start-fired and pre-tool-use-fired during the real session. The fixture used an isolated authenticated Claude config with explicit workspace trust so project hooks were active.
Live test asserted CAS_AGENT_NAME, CAS_AGENT_ROLE=worker, CAS_FACTORY_MODE=1, CAS_FACTORY_WORKER_CLI/model/effort, CAS_ROOT, and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR from production PtyConfig.
Production config cwd pointed to the disposable project, and the follow-up Bash pwd returned that path.
The assistant returned CAS-EF93E-RULE-ONLY-ORBIT, supplied only by the project CLAUDE.md fixture; the prompt and MCP tool list did not include it.
The production Mux::interrupt_and_inject path interrupted an active turn and the assistant returned the redirected CAS-EF93E-RESUMED marker.
The isolated account intentionally links authentication and settings but has no cloud-synced/user skill collision fixture; the run cannot prove precedence against an unavailable cloud-synced skill.
The bounded matrix has no deterministic >2-minute mcp__cas delay fixture; no claim is made about CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS behavior.

evidence.summary: Real Claude Code 2.1.280 PtyConfig::claude matrix passed one guarded live test in 40.51s with a freshly built cas binary, isolated CAS_ROOT, account fixture, hooks, MCP calls, rule canary, and urgent redirect.
